Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 5) demonstrates a widened superior mediastinum and an abnormal bulge of the left cardiac contour, which are classic radiographic signs of traumatic injury to the great vessels (such as rupture of the ascending aorta or pulmonary trunk) following a penetrating stab wound. The "translucent line" likely represents the interface of a mediastinal hematoma or pneumomediastinum associated with this vascular injury, distinguishing it from isolated cardiac chamber lacerations or simple pneumothorax.
